title: Distributional Objectives for VJEPA
content: Variational Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (VJEPA) learns distributions over future latent representations using predictive negative log-likelihood (NLL). We investigate alternative distributional objectives, including continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), Wasserstein distances, and other divergences, focusing on their training requirements and behavior under model misspecification and data contamination. An important distinction is that NLL, CRPS, and kernel-based scores can be trained from individual target samples, whereas directly optimizing many distributional distances requires estimating the distribution of possible targets given the context. We compare selected objectives through population-level analyses and evaluate NLL, CRPS, and MMD using Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture predictors in controlled frozen-encoder experiments. Results show that CRPS and suitably chosen kernel scores resist artificial target corruption better than Gaussian NLL when evaluated against the original clean distribution, but this robustness does not guarantee faithful representation of legitimate rare futures. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating predictive accuracy, calibration, and the representation of multiple plausible futures rather than relying on a single aggregate score.
